title: Interlayer-exciton reservoir bit in a stacked TMD heterobilayer
idea: Stack: no net stored charge + no capacitor. A MoSe2/WSe2 heterobilayer cell stores the bit as a dense cloud of charge-neutral, spatially indirect excitons (electron in one layer, hole in the other) injected by a short forward pulse across a 1-nm hBN spacer; read applies a reverse field that dissociates them into a sensed current pulse. The stored object is neutral, so junction/GIDL leakage has nothing to drain; loss is only recombination, tuned by hBN thickness and twist angle.
why: Removes Cs (fact 1) and the access-leakage tail (fact 3); us-ms retention still needs refresh but at sub-fJ/bit, in atomically thin stackable tiers.

title: Light-gated storage node through a dark-insulating organic photoconductor plug
idea: Stack: no access transistor + no metal wordline. Each node reaches its bitline through a 20-nm deep-HOMO amorphous organic photoconductor plug that is a near-perfect insulator in the dark; a DUV-patterned SiN waveguide per row carries a ~1 ns pulse from an edge micro-LED that opens every plug in that row for read/write. The wordline becomes light instead of a 3 V tungsten line.
why: Attacks fact 3 (no transistor leakage tail; dark current far below a Si junction) and fact 10 (no 3 V wordline CV^2); removes tungsten wordlines; retention could stretch to minutes.

title: FeRh metamagnetic phase bit written by bipolar Peltier pulses
idea: Stack: no spin-polarized current + no tunnel barrier. A 30-nm FeRh dot, Pd/Ir-doped so its first-order antiferro-to-ferromagnetic transition straddles the operating temperature, is bistable inside its ~10-15 K thermal hysteresis; a thermoelectric junction under it heats (one current polarity, writes FM) or Peltier-cools (other polarity, writes AFM). Read is the ~30-50% resistivity difference between the two magnetic phases, with no MTJ stack.
why: Refresh-free two-terminal metallic cell with no MgO/heavy-metal layers (facts 3, 7); needs +/-5 K die temperature control.

title: Neutral-ionic transition co-crystal as an electronic phase bit
idea: Stack: no ferroic layer + no atomic diffusion. A donor-acceptor mixed-stack co-crystal (TTF-chloranil family, chemically pre-compressed with smaller acceptors to lift its neutral-ionic transition near room temperature) holds the bit as neutral vs ionic stacking; a field pulse nucleates an ionic domain (charge transfer ~0.3 to ~0.7 e per pair) that persists inside the first-order hysteresis, read as a >10x conductance/capacitance change. Only fractions of an electron move between neighbor molecules, so intrinsic switching is ps.
why: Storage without capacitor charge (fact 1) and without atomic wear; vapor/solution grown <150 C on any BEOL.

title: Destructive quantum-interference molecular valve as storage-node access
idea: Stack: no semiconductor channel + sub-1-nm access device. The node connects to the bitline through a self-assembled monolayer of meta-linked molecular wires whose transmission sits in a destructive-interference antiresonance at zero gate field (tunneling suppressed 100-1000x beyond length scaling); a gate field shifts the molecular levels out of the dip to open the valve. The access device is one monolayer thick and defined by chemistry, not lithography.
why: Replaces the transistor leakage tail (fact 3) with QI-suppressed tunneling and removes the litho-defined channel (fact 4); 10-100x retention if on/off >1e6 is reachable.

title: Optically stimulated deep-trap bit borrowed from dosimetry crystals
idea: Stack: no electrical leakage path + no ferroic material. As in Al2O3:C dosimeters, the bit is an electron parked in a deep (>1.5 eV) trap of a 20-nm doped oxide pad, written by a UV row-waveguide pulse under bias and read by weak green stimulation that releases a few percent as luminescence onto an integrated photodiode. Deep dosimeter traps hold charge for years at room temperature, so reads are near non-destructive and refresh is unnecessary.
why: No leakage tail (fact 3) and partial non-destructive read (fact 8); speed limited by luminescence lifetime (ns-us).

title: Heater-polarity spin-Seebeck torque writes a perpendicular magnet
idea: Stack: no charge current through the magnet + unipolar drivers only. Two resistive heaters sit above and below a perpendicular magnet on an insulating ferrimagnet spin source; firing the top heater creates a downward thermal gradient whose spin-Seebeck spin current switches the free layer one way, firing the bottom heater switches it the other. Drivers are unipolar row current sinks, and no current crosses the magnet or a barrier.
why: Nonvolatile (no refresh, fact 3), no bipolar write drivers (fact 7), no barrier-breakdown endurance limit; risk is thermal spin-torque efficiency.

title: Anomalous-Nernst thermal readout of a single-layer magnet bit
idea: Stack: no tunnel barrier + no read current through the bit. A single 3-nm Fe3Al film (large anomalous Nernst coefficient, cobalt-free) stores the bit; reading pulses a shared heater to set a vertical temperature gradient, and the sign of the transverse anomalous-Nernst voltage on the bitline gives magnetization direction. The cell has no MgO, no reference layer, no Ru/Ir SAF.
why: Nonvolatile magnetic cell with a ~3-layer stack instead of ~15 and no Ir/Ru/Co; uV signals need integrating sense amps.

title: Leakage-balanced storage node fed by a matched reverse diode
idea: Stack: no new materials + no refresh controller change. The storage junction's reverse saturation leakage to ground is cancelled by a second, geometrically identical reverse-biased diode from a higher rail into the same node, so the node integrates only the mismatch current and drifts ~5-20x slower in either state; both diodes share temperature, so cancellation tracks heat. Tail cells (random trap-assisted leakage) are mapped out by repair.
why: Stretches median retention 5-20x with standard DRAM process (fact 3: refresh share of idle power drops proportionally).

title: Mn4N antiperovskite ferrimagnet cell free of cobalt and platinum
idea: Stack: no cobalt + no platinum-group or rare-earth metals. The bit is a 5-nm Mn4N film (Ni-doped toward magnetic compensation) with perpendicular anisotropy and a tiny net moment, made by reactive nitriding of manganese; low magnetization cuts switching current ~10x and weak stray fields allow tight packing, read by anomalous Hall or TMR. Constituents are Mn and N only.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: removes Co, Pt, Ir, Tb from a nonvolatile working-memory bit; ~10x lower write current.

title: Breathing metal-organic framework pore state as a bistable bit
idea: Stack: store no electrons + solution growth only. A flexible MOF film (MIL-53 family) with a sealed fixed guest load is bistable between open and narrow-pore forms inside its sorption hysteresis; a field/heat pulse flips the framework conformation, and the open vs closed pore changes permittivity ~1.5-2x, read capacitively. The film grows from solution or vapor below 150 C on any BEOL.
why: Zero-charge, zero-retention-power storage with chemistry-defined cells (facts 1, 4); speed (us-ms) is the main risk.

title: Thermoresponsive polymer-brush collapse bit in a sealed nanocell
idea: Stack: no solid-state switching + no atomic diffusion. A grafted polymer brush in a sealed 20-nm solvent-filled cell sits at a coil-globule transition with hysteresis; a heater pulse collapses it (solvent expelled to a reservoir) and a cooling/field pulse re-swells it, and the solvent-vs-polymer permittivity swing at the electrode is read capacitively. Soft-matter states carry no charge to leak.
why: Charge-free storage with near-unlimited endurance (no bond breaking); very slow today (us-ms), speculative for DRAM-class speed.

title: Dislocation-glide bit between two pinning sites in a strained film
idea: Stack: no point-defect motion + no stored charge. A single misfit dislocation in a 15-nm strained SiGe or oxide bridge glides between two engineered pinning sites under a shear-stress pulse from a piezo underlayer; its core changes local band offset and scattering, giving a measurable resistance difference. A dislocation is a line defect pinned by a large Peierls barrier, so the state persists without power.
why: Nonvolatile resistive bit from a crystal defect rather than ions or phases; endurance and reproducibility are open questions.

title: Radical pi-dimer bistability in spiro-biphenalenyl films
idea: Stack: no metal ions + simultaneous electrical, optical and magnetic contrast. Phenalenyl-radical solids switch between pi-dimerized (diamagnetic, insulating) and monomeric (paramagnetic, conducting) states with ~20-30 K hysteresis near room temperature; a 30-nm film per cell is flipped by short heat/field pulses inside the hysteresis window and read by its multi-order conductivity change. Evaporable at low temperature on any substrate.
why: Phase bit made from C/H/O/N only (scarce-resource axis); needs a die temperature inside the hysteresis window.

title: Piezotronic strain-gated Schottky barrier as storage-node access
idea: Stack: no gate oxide + no moving parts. The node contacts the bitline through a ZnO-type piezoelectric semiconductor Schottky contact; at rest the barrier is ~1 eV (leakage negligible), and a row piezo actuator strains the contact so piezo-polarization charge lowers the barrier by ~0.3-0.4 eV, opening it for read/write. Unlike NEMS relays nothing moves; the barrier height itself is the switch.
why: Attacks the access leakage tail (fact 3) and wordline voltage (fact 10) with a stress-gated barrier; 10-100x retention gain claimed.

title: Biomineralized magnetite crystals assembled as litho-free magnetic bits
idea: Stack: no lithography for the storage element + no rare or platinum metals. Magnetotactic-bacteria proteins (Mms6-type, cell-free) mineralize single-domain 35-50 nm magnetite crystals with near-identical size and shape; peptide/DNA affinity tags place one crystal on each DUV crossbar pad, where a Hall/TMR sensor reads it. Biology supplies the precision that EUV would otherwise provide.
why: Nonvolatile bit (~250 kT barrier) built from iron oxide by biomanufacturing; attacks capital intensity and chokepoint metals.

title: Van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2 with hBN barrier cell
idea: Stack: no sputtered amorphous barrier + intrinsic perpendicular anisotropy. Use the room-temperature (Tc ~350-380 K) layered ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2 grown by low-temperature MBE/CVD as both free and fixed electrodes with a 2-3-layer hBN tunnel barrier; atomically sharp interfaces give high spin filtering, and anisotropy is bulk-crystalline so it survives at sub-20-nm dots without interface engineering. No CoFeB, no Ta/W seed, no MgO.
why: Nonvolatile cell with a 3-material stack; removes W/Ta seeds and Co; atomically thin tiers stack well.

title: Microdischarge wall-charge bit borrowed from AC plasma displays
idea: Stack: no solid-state switch + no transistor. Each cell is a sealed micro-cavity of N2/Ar (no helium) with dielectric-coated electrodes; a discharge deposits wall charge that adds to the shared sustain voltage, so ON cells re-fire each sustain cycle and OFF cells stay dark, and state is read from the displacement-current spike. Field-emission-assisted microdischarges below the Paschen minimum are the route to sub-micron cells.
why: Transistor-free bistable memory physics (fact 7 periphery); speculative on density and speed.

title: Metallic-glass fictive-temperature bit without crystallization
idea: Stack: no chalcogenides + no crystallization front. A 10-nm Cu-Zr metallic-glass segment stays amorphous forever; a long sub-Tg pulse relaxes it to a low-energy state and a fast above-Tg pulse with rapid quench rejuvenates it, shifting resistivity and modulus a few percent, read differentially against a twin reference segment. No nucleation, so no stochastic crystal growth or drift from it.
why: Nonvolatile resistive bit in Earth-abundant metals; small contrast (2-5%) is the risk.

title: Emergent interface ferromagnet from C60 on copper as the free layer
idea: Stack: no intrinsically magnetic elements + low-temperature deposition. Charge transfer and hybridization at Cu/C60 (or Sc/C60) interfaces can make non-magnetic metals ferromagnetic at room temperature; use that molecular-interface magnet, evaporated below 100 C, as the free layer of a bit read by tunneling magnetoresistance.
why: Removes Co/Fe/Pt/rare-earths entirely from the storage layer; nonvolatile; speculative on stability at small size.

title: Interlayer-DMI chiral twist between two magnetic layers as the bit
idea: Stack: no reference layer + field-free switching. An in-plane and a perpendicular magnet coupled through a spacer with interlayer Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction favour a left- or right-twisted relative orientation; the bit is the twist sense, toggled by in-plane current spin-orbit torque without field and read by the AMR/TMR difference of the two canted states.
why: New stored degree of freedom (chiral interlayer twist) that is nonvolatile and field-free; speculative.

title: Gate-polarity-selected RKKY exchange writes the free magnet
idea: Free and fixed magnets are separated by a 1-2 nm gated semiconductor/semimetal spacer; one gate polarity shifts the spacer Fermi level so interlayer RKKY coupling turns antiferromagnetic, the other ferromagnetic, dragging the free layer into the chosen state, after which its own anisotropy holds it. No-EUV: 4F2 crosspoint at 20 nm via DUV SAQP (about the density of 6F2 at 16 nm). Zero refresh: nonvolatile, and the write is capacitive with no current through any barrier.
why: Kills refresh (46 fJ/bit, 16-33% idle power; fact 3) and EUV layers (fact 4); fJ capacitive write instead of uA STT currents; unlimited endurance.

title: Magnon current through an insulating conduit writes from a shared source
idea: A row-shared spin source injects angular momentum into a 10-nm insulating magnetic conduit that carries it as magnon current (no electrons) to perpendicular magnets above; the target cell is chosen by a coincident column assist pulse (half-select). No-EUV: every layer is BEOL-sputtered and patterned at >=38 nm DUV half-pitch. Zero refresh: nonvolatile magnets, and no charge current ever crosses a bit.
why: No refresh (fact 3); one spin source serves a whole row, shrinking periphery (fact 7); barrier-free endurance.

title: Heat-only toggle ferrimagnet bit with read-before-write
idea: Each bit is a 25-nm ferrimagnet (Mn2RuxGa, rare-earth-free) that reverses deterministically after any single ~10 ps heating pulse through sublattice demagnetization; the controller reads first and fires a picosecond current pulse in a resistive under-heater only if the bit must change. No-EUV: the heater line is the wordline at DUV pitch, no selector or SOT layer. Zero refresh: magnetization is nonvolatile.
why: ~10-30 fJ write, zero refresh (facts 3, 10); removes W/Pt spin-orbit layers (tungsten chokepoint).

title: Insulating spinel-ferrite bit read by spin-Hall magnetoresistance
idea: The bit is the perpendicular magnetization of a 10-nm MgAl-ferrite (Mg, Al, Fe only) insulator dot under a 2-nm heavy-metal stripe that both writes it by spin-orbit torque and reads it by spin-Hall magnetoresistance. No tunnel barrier, MgO or reference stack. No-EUV: a two-layer stack patterned at 40 nm DUV. Zero refresh: nonvolatile insulator magnet with no shunting current.
why: Nonvolatile cell with a two-layer stack (fewer depositions, no barrier breakdown); Earth-abundant storage layer.

title: Chiral-monolayer charge displacement flips the magnet without current
idea: A self-assembled monolayer of chiral helical oligopeptides on a 2-nm perpendicular magnet, capped by a thin gate dielectric, is pulsed; the displaced charge along the helices is spin-polarized by chiral-induced spin selectivity and exerts exchange torque, and gate polarity selects up or down. No-EUV: the active layer self-assembles; electrodes are DUV crossbars. Zero refresh: the magnet is nonvolatile and the write is capacitive (no DC current).
why: fJ CV^2 write, no STT current, no heavy metals; zero refresh (fact 3).

title: Skyrmion-number bit in block-copolymer-templated magnetic nanodisks
idea: Block-copolymer self-assembly templates 25-nm chiral-multilayer disks; each disk holds topological charge 0 or 1 (one skyrmion), nucleated or annihilated by opposite spin-orbit-torque pulses and read by non-collinear magnetoresistance. No-EUV: sub-20-nm disks come from polymer phase separation under DUV-defined lines. Zero refresh: topological protection adds an annihilation barrier, so the state is nonvolatile below the usual superparamagnetic size.
why: Litho-free sub-20-nm nonvolatile bits (facts 3, 4).

title: Helimagnet spiral handedness bit read by nonreciprocal resistance
idea: The bit is the left/right chirality of a spin spiral in a centrosymmetric near-room-temperature helimagnet (MnAu2-type); a current pulse with a small bias field selects handedness, and electrical magnetochiral anisotropy (resistance differs for +I vs -I) reads it. No-EUV: chirality is a bulk property, so cell size is set by DUV pitch, not magnet stability. Zero refresh: chirality persists with zero stray field, so cells pack without cross-talk.
why: Nonvolatile, stray-field-free, barrier-free storage (fact 3); new stored degree of freedom.

title: Depth-stacked magnetic layers addressed by distinct resonance frequencies
idea: Deposit 8 magnetic layers per pillar, each with a different anisotropy and so a different ferromagnetic-resonance frequency (5-40 GHz); a microwave burst at layer k's frequency plus weak bias switches only layer k, and read senses the layer-resolved resonance shift on a shared inductive line. No-EUV: tiers come from sputter recipes, one DUV pillar patterning for all 8 bits. Zero refresh: every layer is nonvolatile.
why: ~8x bits per DUV feature without per-tier lithography (facts 2, 4); no refresh.

title: Negative-U defect configuration bit with an engineered relaxation barrier
idea: An amorphous oxide channel is seeded with a designed deep donor that has two configurations, shallow (conducting) and large-lattice-relaxation deep (insulating) like a DX center, separated by a ~1.3 eV configurational barrier; an electron-capture pulse turns the channel off and a hole/field pulse turns it on, ~1000x conductance contrast. No-EUV: a vertical, thickness-defined stack in a DUV crosspoint. Zero refresh: the bit is held by atomic configuration, not charge on a leaky node, so retention is years.
why: Removes the capacitor (fact 1) and leakage tail (fact 3) at once; no refresh.

title: Electrically driven diarylethene ring-closure monolayer crosspoint
idea: A self-assembled monolayer of thermally stable P-type diarylethene sits between DUV crossbar electrodes; ring closing and opening are triggered by inelastic-tunneling electrons at two bias thresholds instead of light, and the isomers differ ~100x in conductance. No-EUV: chemistry defines ~1-nm molecular pitch; partial-ensemble fractions give MLC. Zero refresh: both isomers are stable for years at 85 C.
why: Litho-free molecular density with no refresh; molecular fatigue (1e4-1e6 cycles vs DRAM 1e15+) is the key risk.

title: Capillary-condensation hysteresis bit in sealed mesopores
idea: Each cell is a sealed ~5-nm mesoporous-silica pocket holding a fixed vapor inventory chosen inside the capillary-condensation hysteresis loop, so a pore is stably either liquid-filled or empty; a ns heater pulse empties it, a field-assisted nucleation pulse refills it, and the ~20x permittivity contrast is read capacitively. No-EUV: pores self-assemble from surfactant templates. Zero refresh: the state is thermodynamically metastable and needs no power.
why: Charge-free, wear-free storage with litho-free pore density; no refresh (fact 3).

title: Thermionic heat-gated charge node with no access transistor
idea: The storage capacitor is isolated by a ~1.3 eV heterobarrier instead of a transistor; at 85 C thermionic leakage is ~1e-22 A, while a ~5 ns local heating pulse to ~1100 K plus Schottky barrier lowering lets it charge or discharge in ~100 ns. No-EUV: a two-terminal vertical cell in a DUV crosspoint. Zero refresh: years of retention at operating temperature.
why: Removes the access transistor and its leakage tail (fact 3) and its EUV layers (fact 4); risk is pJ heating energy and thermal-cycling endurance.

title: Glancing-angle self-shadowed magnetic nanocolumns as litho-free bits
idea: Oblique deposition onto a DUV-patterned seed grating self-shadows into isolated 10-15 nm magnetic columns with strong shape anisotropy, each a bit contacted top and bottom by DUV crosspoint lines. No-EUV: column pitch is set by self-shadowing below DUV resolution. Zero refresh: column height, not width, sets the thermal barrier, so tiny columns stay nonvolatile.
why: Sub-DUV-pitch nonvolatile bit density without EUV (fact 4); no refresh.

title: Light-ion irradiation defines magnetic bits in an unetched film
idea: A continuous perpendicular multilayer is irradiated with He+ through a DUV-patterned stencil; irradiated regions intermix and lose anisotropy, leaving flat nonvolatile islands in soft moats with no etch damage or redeposition. No-EUV: patterning is by DUV mask plus ions, and the flat surface lets the next tier be deposited directly. Zero refresh: the islands are nonvolatile.
why: Removes magnet ion-beam etch (yield, fact 6) and EUV; enables flat multi-tier stacking.

title: Repurpose HDD bit-patterned-media imprint lines for working-memory magnets
idea: Strategy: the HDD industry has built nanoimprint masters and media sputter tools for ~10-nm bit-patterned media; license or acquire them to imprint 15-20 nm perpendicular magnet arrays on CMOS wafers, wired by DUV crosspoint lines, as a DRAM-class tier. No-EUV: imprint replaces EUV. Zero refresh: the magnets are nonvolatile.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4) and U.S. manufacturability: reuses existing nanoimprint and sputter capacity instead of $15B EUV fabs.

title: SmS valence-transition bit switched by a local stress pulse
idea: A 20-nm SmS film is semiconducting (black, Sm2+) or metallic (gold, mixed valence) with a pressure-driven first-order valence transition whose hysteresis lets the gold phase persist in clamped films at zero stress; a piezo AlN actuator under each DUV cell writes metal with a ~0.7 GPa pulse, and a heat pulse restores the semiconductor, ~1000x resistance contrast. No-EUV: actuators and cells at DUV pitch. Zero refresh: both phases are stable without power, and electrons move 4f to 5d, not atoms.
why: Nonvolatile, diffusion-free resistive bit; Sm use is grams per wafer lot.

title: Thermo-electret frozen-dipole glass gating a thin channel
idea: A high-Tg polar molecular glass (dipolar chromophore in polyimide) sits on a thin MoS2 or poly-Si channel; a heater pulse lifts it above Tg while a gate field orients its dipoles, and cooling freezes the orientation so the built-in polarization shifts the channel threshold. Not ferroelectric: orientation is frozen by glass vitrification. No-EUV: spin-coated film on a DUV transistor. Zero refresh: below Tg the dipoles stay frozen for years.
why: Nonvolatile gain-type cell with no stored charge on a leaky node (facts 1, 3); slow writes are the risk.

title: Four-state biaxial magnet read by planar Hall plus unidirectional magnetoresistance
idea: One 30-nm Fe-based dot with fourfold in-plane anisotropy stores two bits as one of four easy directions; two orthogonal DUV current lines write via vector spin-orbit torque, the planar Hall voltage reads the axis (0/90 deg) and unidirectional spin-Hall magnetoresistance reads its sign. No tunnel barrier. No-EUV: 2 bits per DUV cell. Zero refresh: all four states are nonvolatile.
why: Doubles bits per DUV feature (fact 4) with no refresh (fact 3).

title: Word-plane VCMA select in vertical spin-orbit magnetic strings
idea: Copy 3D-NAND topology: alternate gate-oxide word planes with 2-nm magnet rings around a vertical heavy-metal channel; current down the channel applies spin-orbit torque to every ring, while voltage on one word plane lowers that ring's anisotropy (VCMA) so only it switches, and read selects a plane and senses the channel's magnetoresistance. No-EUV: one DUV channel-hole step serves N tiers. Zero refresh: rings are nonvolatile.
why: 3D memory without a capacitor or lateral transistor (fact 2) and with one litho step for N tiers (fact 4).

title: Frustrated artificial-spin-ice vertex as a multi-level nonvolatile cell
idea: Four nanoimprinted elongated nanomagnets meet at a frustrated vertex; its 16 configurations fall into energy-distinct classes, and a central Hall sensor resolves 4 vertex classes, giving 2 bits per cell, written by programmed field sequences from two crossing lines. No-EUV: nanoimprint plus DUV wiring. Zero refresh: each class is nonvolatile.
why: MLC nonvolatile cell (facts 3, 4) without tunnel barriers.

title: Chemical order-disorder intermetallic bit written by thermal profile
idea: A 20-nm Earth-abundant Ni3Fe/Ni3Mn intermetallic segment stores the bit as ordered vs disordered lattice: a fast quench pulse locks in disorder (high residual resistivity) and a longer moderate pulse reorders it by nearest-neighbor swaps (low resistivity), ~2-3x contrast, with no amorphization, chalcogenides or long-range diffusion. No-EUV: a vertical segment in a DUV crosspoint. Zero refresh: ordering sits behind an ~eV atomic-exchange barrier.
why: Nonvolatile resistive bit from Earth-abundant metals; ordering speed (us) is the risk.

title: Self-reversing ferrimagnet bit written by heat-pulse amplitude alone
idea: Borrow the Haruna dacite titanohematite self-reversal: two exchange-coupled ferrimagnetic phases with different Curie points sit in one nanodot, so a short heat pulse to T1 leaves the high-Tc phase aligned (bit 1) while a hotter pulse to T2 lets the low-Tc phase dominate on cooling and lock the opposite sign (bit 0); read by TMR. No write field and no spin-torque current are needed, only a wordline heater set to two amplitudes.
why: Removes field coils and high-current SOT/STT drivers that bloat periphery (fact 7); write energy is set by heating a ~20 nm dot (~10-50 fJ).

title: Lamellar-magnetism interface bit in ilmenite-hematite superlattice
idea: Copy the stable remanence of exsolved ilmenite-hematite rocks, where net moment lives only in contact layers between two antiferromagnets: grow a short Fe2O3/FeTiO3 superlattice so uncompensated Fe2+/Fe3+ interface layers form the free layer of the bit. The bulk is antiferromagnetic, so there is almost no stray field, coercivity is very high, and cells can be packed tightly.
why: Density: no stray-field crosstalk lets pitch shrink below 20 nm; earth-abundant Fe/Ti instead of Co/Pt/Ir stacks; gigayear-proven thermal stability.

title: Color-center spin-population bit with millisecond DRAM-like retention
idea: Use the spin of NV-type color centers in diamond or SiC (the defects that make minerals glow) as the stored variable: an optical/microwave pulse sets the ensemble spin to ms=0 or ms=+-1, it relaxes with T1 of ~5-10 ms at room temperature, and it is read by spin-dependent photocurrent on a co-integrated contact. Refresh works like DRAM, with no capacitor at all.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) because nothing is stored as charge; the storage element is a ~10 nm defect cluster with no access-transistor leakage tail.

title: Polaron self-deepening trap storage node in Magneli Ti4O7
idea: Store electrons in a thin Magneli-phase titanium-oxide layer where each injected carrier self-traps as a small polaron (bipolaron), distorting the lattice around itself. Leaving then requires undoing that distortion (a Marcus reorganization barrier ~0.5-0.8 eV) on top of the band offset, so the charge digs its own retention well, while a hot-carrier write pulse can still bring charge in quickly.
why: Attacks the leakage tail (fact 3): the extra reorganization barrier could cut detrapping by 10^3x, giving refresh intervals of seconds and saving the 16-33% idle refresh power.

title: Spinodal exsolution grows litho-free nanomagnet arrays
idea: Mimic the cloth-texture exsolution in titanomagnetite, where a magnetic phase separates into regular 10-20 nm rods inside a non-magnetic host: anneal a deposited Fe-Ti-Al spinel film so spinodal decomposition self-assembles a periodic array of shape-anisotropic magnetic rods, each one a bit, registered to a coarse pre-pattern. Lithography only needs to define the wiring pitch, not the bits.
why: Capital: removes 2-3 critical EUV patterning steps for the storage layer (fact 4); the rod pitch is set by thermodynamics, giving sub-20 nm cells.

title: Scaly-foot-snail graded armor sink against row hammer
idea: The deep-vent scaly-foot snail survives attacks with a layered iron-sulfide/organic/aragonite shell that absorbs damage. Copy it by putting a grounded, trap-rich graded layer (doped poly with a defect-rich transition) between neighbouring storage nodes, so the electrons that aggressor rows inject and the coupling fields they cause are soaked up before they reach the victim node.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): raising the flip threshold from ~1k to >50k activations removes TRR/RFM refresh overhead and the bandwidth it costs.

title: Stishovite high-pressure silica as a capacitor dielectric
idea: Meteorite impacts produce stishovite, SiO2 with six-fold Si coordination, k ~9-10 and a bandgap ~8 eV, and it stays metastable at the surface. Make it in capacitor liners by laser-shock or high-pressure plasma densification of ALD SiO2, then quench it under a stressor cap, giving a pure Si-O dielectric with 2.5x the k of silica and a near-perfect interface.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): more charge per area without exotic Hf/Zr/rare elements and with very low leakage; lets Cs ~5 fF at lower aspect ratio.

title: Meteoritic tetrataenite replaces iridium and platinum in magnetic bits
idea: Tetrataenite (L1_0 FeNi) forms in iron meteorites over millions of years and has very high anisotropy with no rare metals. Make it in a minute by nitrogen insertion and extraction (FeNiN to L1_0 FeNi), and use it as the pinned reference and high-anisotropy storage layer of spin-based bits in place of IrMn, Pt/Co multilayers and FePt.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: iridium and platinum are extreme chokepoints; it also allows ~10 nm thermally stable bits (Ku ~1 MJ/m3) for density.

title: Van Allen micro-trap stores free electrons in a magnetic bottle
idea: Copy Earth's radiation belts: a sealed micro-cavity with a magnetic-mirror field from integrated permanent-magnet film poles plus electrostatic end caps traps a small cloud of field-emitted electrons (bit 1) or is empty (bit 0). The cloud is sensed by the image charge it induces on a pickup electrode. There is no solid around the charge, so there is no leakage path except residual gas collisions.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) removed in principle: confinement in vacuum gives retention of seconds or more with no access-transistor junction.

title: Ice-age stochastic resonance reads sub-femtofarad nodes
idea: Glacial cycles respond strongly to weak orbital forcing because noise pushes the climate between states (stochastic resonance). Build the sense element as a deliberately noisy bistable latch biased at its symmetry point, add a periodic dither, and let the tiny storage-node charge (0.5-1 fF) bias the escape statistics; a time-averaged count of switching events decides the bit.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): reading 5-10x smaller Cs removes the need for AR 60-75 pillars, cutting capacitor process steps and allowing 3D tiers.

title: Varistor double-Schottky grain-boundary charge bit
idea: Natural and ceramic zincite (ZnO) varistors show hysteresis because charge trapped in grain-boundary interface states raises the double Schottky barrier. Make one engineered grain boundary per cell and store the bit as interface-state charge (high or low barrier), written by a forward pulse and read non-destructively as boundary conductance through the barrier.
why: Non-destructive read and gain (fact 8): the barrier height changes conductance exponentially (10^2-10^3 on/off) from a few hundred electrons of stored charge.

title: Quasicrystal phason-flip bit from meteoritic icosahedrite
idea: Icosahedrite (a natural Al-Cu-Fe quasicrystal from meteorites) has phason flips, in which an atom jumps between two nearly equivalent sites without breaking long-range order. Use a field- or current-driven phason flip in a nanoscale Al-Cu-Fe(-Ru) quasicrystal grain as the bit, read through the strong change in local electronic density of states (tunnelling conductance).
why: Density: an atomic-scale double-well storage element made of abundant metals, with the barrier set by the quasiperiodic structure rather than lithography.

title: Single-file water-wire dipole bit in a sub-nanometre channel
idea: Like ice, water molecules lined up in single file in a ~0.8 nm channel (a CNT segment or a synthetic aquaporin analog) order their dipoles collectively into one direction. Flipping the whole chain needs a Bjerrum orientational defect to pass through, which gives a well-defined barrier. Store the bit as chain polarity and read it as the polarization charge on a gate.
why: New storage physics: a collective dipole with a tunable barrier set by channel length and an ultra-small footprint, attacking charge-wall area (fact 1).

title: Spin-orbit-driven bubble memory in insulating garnet films
idea: Revive garnet bubble memory with modern physics: grow perpendicular-anisotropy insulating thulium iron garnet, nucleate and move bubble domains by spin-orbit torque from an adjacent W-free heavy-metal-alloy strip (no rotating field coil), and use local pinning wells as fixed bit sites that hold or lack a bubble. Read by spin-Hall magnetoresistance.
why: Energy and periphery: insulating garnet has no Ohmic loss in the medium, and there are no bias magnets or coils; non-volatile bits remove refresh entirely (fact 3).

title: Polyploid storage cell averages out the leakage tail
idea: Deinococcus survives radiation by keeping 4-10 genome copies. Split each bit into 4 tiny sub-nodes, each with its own minimum-size access device, that share charge onto the bitline on read. One sub-node with a tail-leakage transistor only loses a quarter of the signal, so retention is set by the mean leakage, not the worst 13 fA cell.
why: Refresh (fact 3): refresh intervals 4-8x longer by escaping tail statistics, reclaiming 10-20% bandwidth at 32-64 Gb.

title: Geode-style hydrothermal epitaxy of bulk-k perovskite liners
idea: Geodes grow large perfect crystals inward from cavity walls out of hot aqueous fluid. Grow single-crystal SrTiO3/BaTiO3 liners inside capacitor trenches by low-temperature (~180-220 C) hydrothermal epitaxy from a seeded wall, giving bulk-like crystals with k ~200-300 instead of polycrystalline thin films with k ~40-60.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): reaches the k ~70+ target, lifting Cs at today's aspect ratio or holding Cs at half the AR; it is a BEOL-compatible thermal budget.

title: Columnar-basalt contraction cracking defines the cell array
idea: Cooling basalt cracks into hexagonal columns whose pitch scales with layer thickness. Deposit a thin tensile sacrificial film whose controlled thermal or shrinkage contraction cracks it into a hexagonal network, seed the cracks with a coarse pre-pattern, and use the crack lines as isolation trenches between storage nodes. The crack pitch is about 3x the film thickness, so a ~10 nm film gives ~30 nm cells.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): replaces EUV multipatterning of the storage-node layer with a self-organized fracture pattern.

title: Pinned surface nanobubble capacitance bit from cloud-activation hysteresis
idea: Cloud droplets activate only above a critical supersaturation and then persist, which is the Kohler-curve hysteresis. Similarly, a gas nanobubble pinned in a nanopore exists stably once nucleated. Store the bit as the presence or absence of an electrolytically nucleated H2/O2 nanobubble inside a sealed nanopore capacitor. The bubble removes water's k~80 dielectric from the pore, giving a large capacitance change, and a reverse pulse recombines it.
why: New element physics with ~10x capacitance contrast read non-destructively; pinned nanobubbles last for days, attacking refresh (fact 3).

title: Molybdenite polytype switch: electrostatic 2H-to-1T' phase bit
idea: Molybdenite and its tellurium analogs occur as several stacking polytypes. In monolayer MoTe2/MoWTe2 alloys tuned to sit near the phase boundary, gate-injected charge switches the lattice between semiconducting 2H and semimetallic 1T'. The bit is the polytype itself, read as channel conductance with a 10^3 contrast, and written by a field rather than by heat.
why: Energy: a phase-change-class contrast without melt-quench (write ~fJ from capacitive doping); a 2D layer makes it stackable for 3D (fact 2).

title: Supercritical-fluid deposition fills AR-150 capacitor pillars
idea: Hydrothermal vents carry silica and metals in supercritical water, which has no surface tension and diffuses like a gas. Deposit capacitor electrode and dielectric from supercritical CO2 carrying metal-organic precursors, which coats AR >150 holes uniformly where ALD purge times and step coverage fail.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): reaching the AR ~115 that more charge needs, with faster cycle time than ALD at extreme AR, raises Cs about 1.5x.

title: Tsunami-shoaling tapered line gives passive read gain
idea: A tsunami grows in amplitude as it enters shallow water because the impedance of the water column rises. Feed the storage node's charge into a short on-chip tapered transmission line, or a resonant LC section, that steps impedance up toward the sense node, giving passive voltage gain of 3-5x before any transistor.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and voltage floor (fact 10): smaller Cs or lower VARY can be read with the same margin, cutting CV^2 energy.

title: Printed magnetosome-chain ink as bio-grown single-domain bits
idea: Grow magnetotactic bacteria in fermenters to harvest membrane-wrapped chains of 40 nm single-domain magnetite. Ink-jet them into printed wells on a foil and align them along the well with a field during drying. Each chain's collective polarity is one bit, flipped by a printed current strap and read by a printed Hall/AMR sensor strip.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: storage elements grown by microbes at 30 C with no vacuum tools; earth-abundant iron.

title: Tardigrade trehalose-glass gate locks ions in printed transistors
idea: Tardigrades survive by vitrifying their cells in trehalose glass. Print an ion-doped trehalose/sugar-glass gate layer on an organic or oxide TFT: below Tg the ions are frozen in place (retention), while a printed micro-heater lifts the gate a few tens of kelvin above Tg for microseconds so a gate pulse can drift the ions toward or away from the channel, shifting threshold voltage by about 1 V.
why: Leakage (fact 3): glassy immobilization gives retention of hours or more with no junction leakage; gate stacks printed from abundant sugars on R2R lines.

title: Printed persistent-phosphor trap cell read by stimulated luminescence
idea: Natural quartz and feldspar store electrons in deep traps for millennia, which is how luminescence dating works. Screen-print SrAl2O4:Eu,Dy (or Sr2MgSi2O7) persistent phosphor dots over printed photodiodes. A UV microLED or field-injection pulse fills the traps (bit 1), and an IR stimulation pulse releases a luminescence flash that the photodiode counts as the read.
why: Removes access-transistor leakage and the charge wall (facts 1, 3); a fully printable storage layer made of abundant Sr/Al.

title: Zeolite cation-hop dipole bit printed from nanocrystal ink
idea: In zeolites, extra-framework Na+/K+ cations sit in one of two cage sites (site I vs II). An applied field makes them hop collectively, giving a switchable polarization with a barrier set by the cage window. Print a dense nano-zeolite ink as the dielectric of printed MIM capacitors and store the bit as which site the cations occupy, read as a polarization or capacitance offset.
why: New printable storage dielectric made of abundant aluminosilicate; the barrier can be tuned by choosing the cation (Li to Cs) to set retention against write speed.

title: Printed zincite persistent-photoconductivity metastable-donor bit
idea: Solution-processed ZnO nanoparticle films show persistent photoconductivity: oxygen-vacancy donors flip into a metastable ionized configuration with large lattice relaxation, so the conductance stays high for hours. Print ZnO channels with a hot-carrier injector or microLED write and an O2-plasma or field reset, and read the bit as channel conductance non-destructively.
why: Fact 8: non-destructive conductance read; abundant Zn; R2R-printable at <150 C.

title: Greenockite photoconductor access device: retention in the dark
idea: Use cadmium-sulfide (greenockite-like) or ZnO photoconductor stripes as the access device to a printed storage capacitor. In the dark the switch is 10^14-10^16 ohm with no p-n junction to leak, and a printed microLED or OLED row flash turns it on for writing and reading. Storage nodes sit in light-tight, cave-dark pockets.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): no junction leakage, so the dark resistance gives retention of seconds or more on printed electronics.

title: Archaeal tetraether lipid monolayer as a printed capacitor dielectric
idea: Archaea in boiling acid springs use membrane-spanning tetraether lipid monolayers that let almost no ions through. Self-assemble synthetic bipolar tetraether lipids (or thiol-anchored analogs) by dip or slot-die coating into a 3-4 nm, pinhole-tolerant dielectric on printed electrodes, giving ~6-8 fF/um2 with very low leakage.
why: Capacitance per area and leakage for printed memory at R2R speed, with no ALD or vacuum tools (capital).

title: Stalactite meniscus-electrodeposited high-aspect pillars for printed capacitors
idea: Stalactites grow tall from slow drip-wise deposition. Print capacitor electrodes the same way, using meniscus-confined electrodeposition from a nozzle array: a tiny electrolyte meniscus pulled upward continuously plates copper or nickel pillars at AR >50 with no etching. A conformal printed or sprayed dielectric and counter-electrode then complete the 3D capacitor.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) without high-AR etch tools; additive, low-capital, US-manufacturable pillar formation.

title: Blocking-temperature-multiplexed printed nanoparticle multilevel magnet
idea: Paleomagnetists recover several field records from one rock because grain populations unblock at different temperatures. Print a dot that mixes magnetite or ferrite nanoparticle inks with 3 distinct blocking temperatures, in volume ratios of 4:2:1. Write the stack hottest-first, heating to each window and cooling in a +/- bitline field, then read 3 bits at once as the net magnetization on a printed sensor.
why: Density: 3 bits per printed element with a non-destructive analog read; inks are cheap and earth-abundant.

title: Roll-to-roll nanoimprinted artificial spin-ice vertex-charge bit
idea: Like natural pyrochlore spin ice, a kagome lattice of nanomagnet islands made by R2R nanoimprint carries emergent monopole charges (+-3, +-1) at its vertices. Store the bit as the magnetic-charge state of a designated vertex, set by a printed current line, protected by the ice rules, and read by a printed magnetoresistive sensor.
why: R2R nanoimprint replaces EUV for the bit layer (capital, fact 4); topologically protected states give robust retention.

title: Depositional-remanence nanorod rotor locked in a printed matrix
idea: Sediments record the geomagnetic field when settling magnetic grains align before compaction locks them. Print elongated magnetic nanorods in a thermoplastic matrix with low Tg: a heat pulse softens the matrix locally, a bitline field rotates the rods to 0 or 180 degrees, and cooling locks them. The bit is the physical rod orientation, read by a printed sensor.
why: Unlimited-retention printed storage element using a rotational degree of freedom, with no transistor leakage path; all-additive.

title: Lightning-implanted space-charge electret gate on printed transistors
idea: Lightning leaves Lichtenberg trees of charge trapped in insulators for years. Print a fluoropolymer (CYTOP- or PTFE-like) electret gate layer, inject a packet of space charge by a short high-field pulse from a printed sharp-edge electrode, and let the trapped charge shift the printed TFT threshold. A reverse corona-like pulse neutralizes it.
why: Printable gate-stack memory with very deep polymer traps for retention; no ALD oxides needed.

title: Embossed nanofluidic concentration-polarization bistable channel
idea: The Atlantic overturning circulation has two stable states set by salt-advection feedback. A nanochannel junction between charged and neutral segments shows the same kind of feedback through ion concentration polarization, giving hysteretic depleted (low-G) and enriched (high-G) states. R2R-emboss the nanochannels in polymer, fill them with a gel electrolyte, and read the bit as junction conductance.
why: New printable bistable storage physics whose state is maintained by a feedback loop rather than a barrier; fully R2R-compatible.

title: Ooid-style core-shell nanocapacitor particles printed onto transistor arrays
idea: Ooids grow as concentric shells around a nucleus. Synthesize colloidal metal-core / high-k-shell / conductive-outer-shell spheres, each a complete ~10 fF capacitor. Print or directed-assemble one into each well of a printed TFT backplane, so capacitors are made in a reactor in bulk instead of on the wafer.
why: Capital: moves the capacitor module off the fab into colloid chemistry; capacitance per footprint from 3D spherical shells.

title: Global-electric-circuit AC rail self-sustains printed storage nodes
idea: Earth's thunderstorms keep the ionosphere charged against constant leakage. Give each printed node one extra printed TFT whose gate is the node, connecting a global pulsed AC rail through a printed diode back to the node. A '1' node is topped up on every rail pulse and a '0' node stays off, so leaky printed transistors no longer need refresh cycles.
why: Makes leaky printed TFTs (pA-nA) usable as DRAM; refresh bandwidth and controller logic disappear (fact 3).

title: Thermophilic photosynthetic reaction-center charge-separated bit ink
idea: Hot-spring purple bacteria build reaction centers that separate charge across a protein in picoseconds, and the P+QB- state lasts about 1 s. Print engineered, thermostable reaction centers oriented on electrodes: light or an electrical pulse writes the charge-separated state, it is read as a photovoltage or capacitance step, and a quinone-site mutant stretches retention.
why: Picosecond write with seconds of retention from a self-assembled protein storage element printed at room temperature; no fab capital.

title: Pumice-like ferroelectret foam: micro-plasma-switched void dipoles
idea: Volcanic pumice is full of sealed gas voids. In R2R-made cellular polymer foam, applying a field above the Paschen threshold ignites a micro-discharge in each void that deposits opposite charges on the void walls, creating a macro-dipole. A reverse field above threshold flips it, giving ferroelectric-like hysteresis without any polar crystal; read as remanent charge.
why: A printable, polar-crystal-free switchable dipole element made from commodity polymers and air; R2R throughput.

title: Liesegang reaction-diffusion precipitates self-pattern printed cell arrays
idea: Agate banding and Liesegang rings form when diffusing reactants precipitate periodically. Print a gel containing one reactant, flood it with the other, and use the self-organized periodic precipitate dots or lines (metal or metal-oxide) as storage-node electrodes, with the pitch set by gel chemistry rather than masks.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): mask-free, sub-micron periodic storage-element patterning on R2R lines.

title: Silicatein enzyme-mineralized high-k dielectric printed at room temperature
idea: Deep-sea glass sponges build silica skeletons at 4 C with the enzyme silicatein, which can also mineralize titania and barium titanate. Print silicatein-functionalized templates onto capacitor electrodes and bath them in molecular precursors to grow crystalline perovskite dielectric layers at <40 C, with no high-temperature anneal.
why: Brings high-k storage dielectrics to plastic or R2R substrates and cuts energy and capital for dielectric formation.

title: Orpiment-glass valence-alternation-pair photodarkening bit
idea: The arsenic-sulfide minerals orpiment and realgar change structure under light. Spin- or slot-die-coated chalcogenide glass (As2S3, or GeS2 in As-free versions) forms metastable valence-alternation defect pairs under a bandgap light or carrier-injection pulse, shifting its conductance and absorption. A mild heat pulse anneals the pairs away; read the bit as photoconductance.
why: A printable storage element with no crystallization step (unlike PCM), so it needs lower write energy; solution-processable glass.

title: Field-switched breathing-framework dielectric printed from MOF ink
idea: Like clay that swells in hydration steps, flexible frameworks (MIL-53-type) switch between large-pore and narrow-pore phases with hysteresis. Print a MOF film as the dielectric of a printed capacitor, switch its pore phase with an electric field (dielectric-energy-driven breathing), and read the bit as the 10-30% capacitance change between the phases.
why: A bistable, printable dielectric storage element whose two phases are separated by a structural barrier; made from abundant Al/Fe and organics.

title: Hammer-pumped cell turns neighbor activations into free refresh
idea: Paradox: disturbance as maintenance. Each storage node gets a tiny asymmetric MIM tunnel rectifier capacitively coupled to the adjacent wordline; every neighbor activation (the row-hammer aggressor pulse) injects a sub-fC packet that the rectifier steers toward the node's current rail (up if above VARY/2, down if below), so ordinary traffic restores both states instead of eroding them.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3) and row hammer (fact 9) become one mechanism; idle rows need only a background dummy toggle at ~1/100 refresh energy; claims 80-90% refresh elimination.

title: Hot-spot latch: suspended nanobridge holds the bit as temperature
idea: Hot AND cold at the same bias: a phonon-isolated 20 nm doped-Si nanobridge with negative TCR in series with a load has an S-shaped electrothermal I-V with two stable temperatures (ambient vs +40 K); the bit is the thermal state, held statically with no access-device leakage and read as resistance. Data are sparse-coded so only ~1 in 16 bridges is ever hot, bounding standby power.
why: Removes the capacitor and the leakage-tail refresh (facts 1,3); single patterned line at relaxed pitch; ~5-10 nW per hot bit, ~0.5 nW/bit averaged under sparse code.

title: Capillary-condensation nanopore: liquid and vapor bit in one pore
idea: Thermodynamic hysteresis as storage: a sealed 5-10 nm pore with attolitres of working fluid sits as either condensed liquid (high-k) or vapor at the same T and P because capillary condensation/evaporation is hysteretic. A 2 ns Joule pulse in the pore wall evaporates it (0), a field pulse nucleates condensation (1); the pore is the capacitor dielectric so C swings ~10-30x.
why: Large read signal without high-AR pillars (fact 1); state held thermodynamically, no refresh; pore arrays etched in sacrificial films without EUV.

title: Breathing-MOF cell: one framework both open and closed
idea: A flexible metal-organic framework film (MIL-53 type) switches between large-pore and narrow-pore phases with wide hysteresis; a field pulse (dielectric-driven breathing) flips it, changing thickness and permittivity of a nanoscale capacitor/FET gate stack, read as ~2x capacitance or a Vt shift. Both phases are stable unpowered.
why: Static bit, no leakage refresh; <300 C solution/ALD process over CMOS; Al/Zn/terephthalate chemistry avoids chokepoint metals; density set by ~10 nm grains.

title: Supercooled nanodroplet bit: frozen and molten at one temperature
idea: Solid AND liquid: an encapsulated 15 nm In-Sn nanodroplet supercools by >100 K, so at 85 C it sits indefinitely as either solid or metastable liquid. Write liquid with a 1 ns melt pulse to ~170 C (vs ~600 C for PCM), write solid with a strain/field nucleation pulse from a piezo seed, read the solid/liquid resistivity or capacitance difference.
why: Static storage with ~5-10x lower write energy than PCM thanks to low melt point, no chalcogenide; refresh-free (fact 3); Sn-Bi variants to limit indium.

title: SmS valence-switch bit: one compound, two valences
idea: Samarium monosulfide flips from semiconducting Sm2+ to metallic Sm3+-like under ~0.6 GPa with large hysteresis; a thin SmS layer clamped to an AlScN piezo actuator gets a 1 ns stress pulse to go metallic and stays metallic after release until a reverse/thermal pulse restores it. Read: >10x resistance contrast.
why: Electronic (not atomic-diffusion) transition: sub-ns switching, high endurance in principle; static, refresh-free, sidesteps capacitor scaling (fact 1).

title: FeRh metamagnetic bit: magnetic and nonmagnetic in one film
idea: Equiatomic FeRh has a first-order AFM-to-FM transition (tunable to ~100 C by Pd/Ir doping) with ~10 K hysteresis; bias the array inside the loop so both phases are stable, write FM with a short heat pulse and AFM with a strain pulse from a piezo underlayer, and read the ~30-40% resistivity drop of the FM phase.
why: Static bit read as plain resistance, no MTJ/MgO stack; write energy set by small latent heat; refresh-free. Rh scarcity addressed by screening Rh-free metamagnets (e.g. Mn3GaC).

title: Heat-toggle ferrimagnet: random heat pulse yields deterministic flip
idea: Disorder creates order: a GdFeCo ferrimagnet toggles magnetization under a single ~ps heat pulse because Gd and Fe sublattices demagnetize at different rates; each cell gets a picosecond electrical pulse from an on-chip step-recovery/photoconductive generator and is read by a small anomalous-Hall cross, with read-before-write giving set/reset. No field, no spin current.
why: Write ~10-30 fJ independent of thermal-stability factor and without a tunnel junction; static, refresh-free; Gd supply mitigated by rare-earth-free ferrimagnet search.

title: Percolation bit in manganite where metal and insulator coexist
idea: In phase-separated (La,Pr,Ca)MnO3 metallic and insulating nanodomains coexist; the bit is whether a metallic percolation path joins two contacts 30 nm apart. A current pulse aligns metallic clusters into a path (1), a reverse/thermal pulse breaks it (0); the glassy phase-separated state freezes the path. Read: orders-of-magnitude resistance contrast.
why: Huge read margin from a ~30 nm capacitor-free element; collective percolation switching in ns; static.

title: Work-function memory gate: a metal surface that remembers
idea: A transistor gate whose underside carries a sub-monolayer of Cs/Ba adatom dipoles in a sealed 1 nm cavity; a gate pulse drives field-induced surface diffusion of adatoms between the gate face (lowers effective work function ~1 eV) and a remote reservoir pad, shifting Vt by hundreds of mV. Retention comes from adatom binding barriers, not trapped charge.
why: Gain-cell read with no storage capacitor and no tunnel-oxide wear; dipoles do not drain through the junction leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Contaminant-as-storage: heater-gated mobile-sodium threshold bit
idea: Turn the classic MOS killer into the bit: a 4 nm gate oxide deliberately doped with Na+/K+; a local 1 ns heater pulse raises ion mobility ~1e5x so a gate bias parks the ion sheet at the channel interface (low Vt) or the gate interface (high Vt). At room temperature the ions freeze, retaining the bit for days; read via Vt.
why: Capacitor-free gain cell; retention decoupled from leakage tail (fact 3); materials are sodium and SiO2, zero chokepoint.

title: Nanofluidic diode bit: water channel remembers ion polarization
idea: A sealed 5 nm asymmetric nanochannel filled with dilute electrolyte acts as a memristive ionic diode: a voltage pulse builds ion-concentration polarization (depletion or enrichment) that persists because back-diffusion is blocked by a charged gate segment; read by channel conductance. Wet electronics on a dry chip.
why: Capacitor-free, long-retention bit from SiN channels and salt water; ~fJ writes; tests whether ionic memory can reach 100 ns.

title: Glass-frozen dipole electret: liquid when written, solid when stored
idea: A 5 nm side-chain polymer dielectric with strong dipoles and Tg ~200 C: a 1 ns heater pulse lifts the film above Tg while a bias poles dipoles up or down; cooling in ns freezes the orientation, giving remanent polarization without a ferroelectric. Read nondestructively as the Vt shift of the underlying transistor.
why: Polarization bit without ferroelectric wake-up/fatigue or HZO; spin-on, BEOL-compatible; capacitor-free (fact 1).

title: Light-fed latch: global illumination sustains dynamic cells
idea: Static AND dynamic: each storage node gates a tiny phototransistor that, under a uniform backside near-IR flood through a Ge absorber, sources photocurrent back into the node only when the node is already high; a 0 node keeps it off. One optical bias replaces per-row refresh.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) moved to a single optical bias touching all rows at once; cell stays near 1T1C plus one weak device.

title: Chirality bit: left- and right-handed tellurium in one nanocrystal
idea: Trigonal tellurium is chiral; in a 10 nm clamped Te nanocrystal the bit is the handedness, switched by a current pulse that melts the core while a chiral-seed electrode or spin-polarized current selects which enantiomer recrystallizes. Read via handedness-dependent nonreciprocal (magnetochiral) resistance.
why: Mirror states have identical energy and structure, so no drift; static bit; Te is a copper-refining by-product with US supply.

title: Frustrated spin-ice vertex: disorder pinned as an ordered bit
idea: In a four-nanomagnet artificial-spin-ice vertex, frustration makes the monopole (3-in/1-out) configuration metastable; the bit is whether a monopole charge sits on the vertex or is expelled, injected by a current-line field pulse and read by a local Hall bar. Hopping barriers are set by island geometry, not single-magnet volume.
why: Collective frustration supplies retention so each island can be smaller than a thermally stable single magnet; static, refresh-free.

title: Twist-lock bit: 2D flake rotation locked at commensurate angles
idea: A 20 nm graphene flake on a superlubric hBN base rotates almost freely except at commensurate 0/60 degree locks; the bit is which lock it occupies, kicked by a short in-plane field on a polar edge and read via moire-dependent tunnelling conductance. Free AND locked: superlubricity makes switching cheap, commensuration makes it stable.
why: Mechanical-state bit with no capacitor and wear-free superlubric contact; static.

title: Skyrmion-bag counter: one magnetic bubble holds several topological charges
idea: A skyrmion bag (outer skyrmion enclosing N inner ones) in a chiral multilayer dot stores log2(Nmax) bits as its topological degree; spin-orbit pulses add or extract inner skyrmions through a notch, and topological Hall voltage reads N. Many AND one: a single boundary with discrete, topology-protected levels.
why: Multiple bits per ~50 nm dot, static; discrete levels without precise analog charge (fact 1 density).

title: Self-squeezing dielectric: a charged cell lowers its own voltage
idea: Capacitor dielectric is a compressible van der Waals gap layer: storing a 1 electrostatically squeezes the gap ~15%, raising C, so the same charge sits at lower voltage; since junction/GIDL leakage is exponential in voltage, the charged state leaks several times less. The more charge, the less it wants to leave.
why: State-dependent nonlinear capacitance attacks the refresh tail (fact 3) and charge wall (fact 1); claims 3-5x retention at equal footprint.

title: Electrofrozen water bit: ice at room temperature in a nanogap
idea: Water confined in a templated 2 nm hydrophilic gap freezes into a polar ice phase under ~1 V/nm (electrofreezing); surface templating keeps the ice metastable after the field drops and a heat pulse melts it. Read: liquid vs ice permittivity gives a large capacitance swing.
why: Static bit whose only active material is water; zero chokepoint; large signal without high-AR capacitor.

title: Neutral-ionic crystal bit: same lattice both neutral and ionic
idea: Mixed-stack donor-acceptor co-crystals (TTF-CA family, engineered to transition near room temperature) switch between neutral and ionic (dimerized, polar) phases with hysteresis; a field pulse drives the transition domain by domain and the ionic phase's higher conductivity/permittivity is read by a small FET.
why: Electronic-structural transition switches in ps-ns; static bit from solution-processable organic crystals with no chokepoint metals.
